edges.effect_quant: Across modern diagnostic studies, self-collected HPV testing is close to clinician-collected testing for detecting CIN2+ or worse, especially with PCR-based assays. The 2025 meta-analysis found pooled sensitivity of 90% for self-collected HPV testing versus 93% for clinician-collected HPV testing, both higher than clinician-collected cytology at 87%.
edges.population: women eligible for cervical cancer screening using high-risk HPV testing, especially those considering self-collected vaginal or urine sampling
edges.mechanism: Self-collected HPV DNA testing can identify high-risk HPV infection and associated precancerous lesions without requiring a speculum exam, which can expand acceptable access to molecular cervical screening and preserve high diagnostic sensitivity when validated assays are used.
edges.summary: This edge is now stronger than older summaries made it seem. The literature has moved from asking whether self-sampling is merely feasible to showing that validated HPV assays on self-collected specimens can approach clinician-collected performance closely enough to support real-world screening and lesion detection.
edges.caveats: Performance depends on assay platform, specimen type, and population. Much of the strongest evidence is about detection of CIN2+ or CIN3+ as a surrogate for cervical cancer detection rather than direct mortality outcomes, and some urine-based approaches remain slightly less sensitive than clinician-collected cervical samples.

evidence.citation: Arbyn M et al 2014 Lancet Oncol
evidence.notes: Accuracy of human papillomavirus testing on self-collected versus clinician-collected samples: a meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: absolute sensitivity of self-sampled HPV testing for CIN2+ in screening settings; PCR-based assays approached clinician-collected accuracy more closely
